trails.title: Whose Nightmare?
trails.description: They're not only sealed in archives.

content.text: Excerpt from the Vampire Beyond Entity File

File No.: XXX-1912-B (The Beyond - Vampire)

Clearance Level: Top Secret

The vampire is an extremely rare Beyond being bearing a strong resemblance to humans, yet with several defining traits: its skin is notably pale, its irises typically crimson—varying in depth with its tolerance for blood intake. Anatomical studies confirm that blood functions as one of its key energy sources. Vampires exhibit a compulsive craving for blood, particularly that of highly active animals.

Key Traits:

1. Bloodthirst

A vampire's obsession with blood often triggers bouts of extreme aggression and heightened tracking ability (showing acute sensitivity to the scent of blood). However, certain reports suggest blood is not their sole means of sustenance. A rare few can resist Bloodthirst altogether or survive on alternative food sources without dependence on blood.

2. Photophobia

Vampires exhibit a marked physiological aversion to sunlight. Prolonged exposure to strong daylight causes irreversible tissue damage. These entities cast no visible shadows or reflections—whether upon water, glass, mirrors, or polished metal surfaces.

3. Vulnerabilities

Ordinary physical attacks are largely ineffective. Only bullets forged from metals refined through specific alchemical techniques (most notably pure silver) can inflict permanent injury upon them.

4. Vampire Infected

When a vampire bites or exchanges bodily fluids with an individual possessing innate arcanum affinity, there is a high probability of "conversion."
The infected undergo █–█ hours of violent physiological and psychological mutation, with a 93% mortality rate and over 96% incidence of mental instability among survivors. Those who endure the process ultimately become "the Infected," gradually gaining the creature's biological traits and mastering its arcane skills.

Note: Intelligence suggests "Manus Vindictae" is conducting ongoing experiments to convert ordinary humans directly into vampires. The success rate and stability of such transformations remain unknown.

Disclaimer

Both vampires and their infected derivatives are officially classified by the Foundation as "the Beyond," distinct from both humans and arcanists.

Last Updated: November 15, 1912

items.text: Dinner arrives, and the tension eases. They hunch over their trays to eat, drink, and chatter, laughter rising and falling.
Of course, there are a few "incidents."

items.speaker: Sonya
items.text: You call this beef stew?

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: I truly am sorry, madam. I'm afraid the war has limited our ability to procure supplies up to our usual standards. It may taste slightly different from our usual fare.

items.speaker: Sonya
items.text: "Slightly different"? This is boiled cowhide in a thin gruel!
She slams her knife and fork down in anger.

items.speaker: Sonya
items.text: It's always "war this" and "war that" with you people. Excuses piled on excuses!

items.speaker: Sonya
items.text: I paid my fare, the same as usual; I deserve the service I've come to expect.

items.speaker: Hatted Gentleman
items.text: Wouldn't you say that's a touch harsh, ma'am?

items.speaker: Hatted Gentleman
items.text: There's people out there gettin' shelled to kingdom come beggin' for any scraps they can get.

items.speaker: Sonya
items.text: Hah! Isn't this what you Brits do—stick your noses into a lady's business and levy pointless accusations? Don't you have something better to do with your miserable little life?

items.speaker: Sonya
items.text: Perhaps you ought to try feeling the sun on your skin, or, I don't know, cooking a meal that doesn't taste like wet socks?

items.speaker: Arbuthnot
items.text: Oh, that's rich, you—
The gentleman flushes red and rises. A stifled giggle sounds behind him.
A woman sits behind them, scribbling purposefully as they speak.

items.speaker: Arbuthnot
items.text: What're you doin', ma'am?
Me? Just recording what I see.
The editor closes her notebook with grace.
"Train Clash: Beef Stew Sparks National Conflict! Lady Accuses British Gent of Abominable Cooking" ...
Or perhaps, "Battle at the Dinner Table: One Woman's Rage over Beef Stew."
Don't let me stop you. This is all excellent material.

items.speaker: Sonya
items.text: Hmph. Journalists ...

items.speaker: Verity
items.text: That I am. Though, I'm primarily an editor. But I write reports whenever a good one comes along. Call me Verity.

items.speaker: Verity
items.text: If you have any interesting material, especially about arcanists, please contact me. I will pay accordingly.
The pair falter, unable to reply, and return to their dinner. The quarrel, now soothed, leaves the stewardess effusively grateful.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Thank you ever so much, madam.

items.speaker: Verity
items.text: Don't you worry, poor thing.
The editor props her head in one hand, turning to watch a passenger feasting in the corner.

items.speaker: Verity
items.text: At least someone's enjoying the meal.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: *munching* I haven't had food like this in *gulp* forever!
The sight of food, real food, melts away the girl's anxieties.
The speed and ferocity with which she eats is startling, yet the investigator spies a curious inconsistency—good table manners.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Thank you, ma'am!

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: It's Semmelweis.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Has anyone ever told you that your eye color is very unique?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Yeah? Uh, thanks.
Rubuska lifts her head, eyes shadowed by her brim—unusual eyes.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: You were saying that this train isn't as safe as it looks.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Why'd you say that, exactly?
She presses her hat lower.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: People rarely match their deeds to their words. They may say one thing, but I've found their true motives to often be much darker.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Anyone could be a danger. The passengers, the conductress, or even ...

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: You.
Her tone is not forceful, falling short of accusation, still Rubuska cannot help but make her case.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Ms. Semmelweis, all I am is a hungry kid looking for food. Look at me, how could I be a threat to anyone?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: You did take that woman's train ticket, yes?
Her voice is gentle, but her words piercing.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: I ... Well, yeah, I took it.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: But, I hadn't eaten anything for four days. I needed to do something to survive.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: I didn't mean to do her any harm. I figured maybe they'd let her on anyway, and then we'd both get on, and there'd be no trouble.
The girl flushes red. Semmelweis holds her stare, as if already knowing the truth and waiting for a confession.
At last, she allows a smile to slip from her face.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: No one can blame you for trying to survive in these conditions. At the very least, you weren't the cause of any harm.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: But there is one thing I'm curious about. How did you reach that ticket earlier? It was your arcane skill, wasn't it?
Her silence is the answer. Realizing her slip, she stiffly changes the subject.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: "People rarely match their deeds to their words," then, what about you? What are you doing here?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I'm here to investigate this "duplicity."
She sidesteps the question, producing a folder from her briefcase.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: But our arrangement was for you to answer the questions.
She draws out a white slip of paper.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Have you seen this pattern before?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Hmm.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Yeah ... Yeah, I've seen it. Maybe in a market? Uh, or, on a wall somewhere.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: I might be able to search my memory more carefully, that is, if you let me go later.
The girl eyes the symbol again, as if thinking hard. But the facade drops.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: You're quite clever. Unfortunately, your acting skills could use a little work, which means I already have my answer.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: You're not one of them.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: *sigh*
She frowns bluntly.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: One last question. How familiar are you with vampiric legends?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: It's often said that their eyes have a peculiar quality, just like ...
She meets the girl's crimson eyes, catching a flicker of panic.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: I-I have no idea what you're talking about.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Excuse me, madam. A moment of your time.
A voice cuts the tension. At the far end of the carriage, the conductress raises a hand, beckoning the investigator.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Stay put. I'll be back soon. Do exactly as a good little assistant would do, understood?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Vampires aren't the only dangerous things that may lurk on this train.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Sure thing, boss—
After warning her "assistant," the investigator rises and makes her way toward the conductress.
Conductress's Cabin

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: That girl is not your assistant.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Save your explanation. I doubt you've known each other for more than half an hour.
The conductress leans against the wall in what must, for her, be a supremely exaggerated gesture.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I wouldn't have expected you to probe into matters of passenger privacy. I believe we should abide by certain basic humanitarian principles, even during wartime. Wouldn't you agree, Conductress?

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: If you were an ordinary passenger, as you claim, I wouldn't have "probed."

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: But you are from that "Foundation," correct?
Her gaze falls on the badge at the investigator's chest.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: That badge with the black-and-white print. Wherever the Foundation shows up, trouble follows.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: No need to be nervous, ma'am. I'm just on my way to Vienna for a little holiday.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Aboard an express train bound to pass through a war zone—you must take your vacations very seriously.
The investigator sighs and pulls out her Foundation ID.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: St. Pavlov Foundation. I'm sure you'll find my identification is in order.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: St. Pavlov Foundation ...

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Investigator Semmelweis.
The conductress returns the card without a change in tone.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: I see. Is there anything that I might do for you, Investigator?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: We've received intelligence that there may be a dangerous vampire on this train. I could use your help in the investigation.
She cuts straight to the point, stating her mission boldly and without restraint.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: A vampire.
A grim shadow passes over the conductress's face.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: You're chasing fairy stories. If you ask around, all you'll get is a hundred different stories; none of them real.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: I can't help you chase a myth.
She returns to the sofa, picking up a pair of knitting needles.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Please have a seat, Investigator. I hope my handicraft doesn't bother you.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: W-What are you working on?

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: A scarf for Aima.
Semmelweis steadies herself, forcing her eyes away from the flickering needles.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I've been tasked with verifying the authenticity of this intelligence. However, your attitude ...
A thought flashes through her mind.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: You mentioned that you've seen this badge and pattern before. Was it someone you met recently?

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: I have worked on the "Danube Dawn" for many years, Investigator. I have seen everything except a vampire.
The conductress lifts her eyes from the tight stitches to meet hers.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I see.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Then let's presume you're telling the truth. It's understandable that it would be difficult to imagine something you've never seen.
The investigator leans forward.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: According to our intel, vampires are extremely dangerous creatures. Once bitten, death is a near certainty, regardless of whether the victim is human or arcanist.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Those few who survive become what is known as "Infected."

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: They're like a bomb with a broken fuse, no predicting when they'll go off.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Therein lies our problem, Conductress. We believe one such vampire is hiding somewhere on this train.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: There's no need to exaggerate the threat this may pose to your passengers. You aren't going to turn a blind eye now, are you?

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Conductress, the station staff said they want to confirm something in person with—Huh?

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: The two women sit facing one another, their expressions cold and serious.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Oh, am I interrupting something important? My apologies, I'll just ...

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Wait. I'll go with you.
The conductress sets the scarf on the sofa's edge.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Excuse me for a moment, Investigator.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: It's an administrative process for the passenger who fell on the tracks.
"Administrative process." She stresses the words.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Let's go. Best not to keep them waiting.
She leaves through the open door, her stewardess trailing behind like a lost duckling.
Semmelweis watches the guards on the platform, studying the movement of their lips.

items.speaker: Platform Guard
items.text: Our supervisors need an answer.

items.speaker: Platform Guard
items.text: The train can't depart unless ...

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Are they trying to blackmail her? I suppose it isn't unheard of in times of war.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: A long stop could prove helpful to my investigation.
Unexpectedly, the conductress does not resist the guards' demands. Instead, she produces a badge.

items.speaker: Platform Guard
items.text: Oh, so you're one of us, hahahahaha.
The standoff ends. A faint smile creeps over Corvus's face.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Could the railway be working with the army? No, then this conversation wouldn't be happening.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Is she handing him a badge?
Then, as if sensing her eyes, the conductress suddenly turns to the window.
Her smile collapses in an instant.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Perceptive, aren't you?
She leans back, watching as the conductress and stewardess disappear from view.
On the steps of the train, the conductress halts and waves her hand briskly.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Alert the station to begin sanding the tracks. We're departing soon.
